newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin has signs of pneumonia, ordered to hospital.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin has signs of pneumonia, ordered to hospital.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin, who had multiple heart surgery two months ago, has developed early signs of pneumonia and doctors have ordered him to go back to hospital, the Kremlin said on Wednesday.
A Kremlin statement said Yeltsin, 65, had been ordered to go to the Central Clinical Hospital in Moscow where he spent time recuperating from his quintuple bypass on November 5.
The president had already cancelled all appointments since Monday because of what the Kremlin said was a heavy cold.
"Doctors have stated that the first signs of pneumonia developing have appeared," the statement said.
"In connection with this, in order to make a better diagnosis and to conduct appropriate treatment, a decision has been taken to take him to the Central Clinical Hospital for several days."
It was not immediately clear if Yeltsin, who has suffered at least two heart attacks, had already been taken to hospital. An official at the hospital decliend to give any information.
Yeltsin had been resting at a country residence outside Moscow because of his illness. Doctors had been due to examine the president on Wednesday afternoon and release a medical bulletin.

Renat Akchurin, the Russian surgeon who led the team that operated on Yeltsin's heart, had told Itar-Tass news agency earlier on Wednesday that the cold was not related to the bypass operation and posed no threat to his heart.
To suggest otherwise was "pure speculation", he said.

The president returned to work in the Kremlin on December 23. He had been holding regularly meetings since then, including having talks with German Chancellor Helmut Kohl last Saturday, at which the Kremlin leader looked pale and tired.

His last announced meetings were on Monday, when he discussed relations with NATO with top Russian leaders and security officials and held a separate meeting with Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin -- his constitutional number two.
Chernomyrdin had been due to start a brief leave on Wednesday but it was not clear if he had left Moscow.
Yeltsin's absence fuelled a struggle for position among Kremlin officials that culminated in the October sacking of security adviser Alexander Lebed amid charges of coup plots.
Chief Kremlin doctor Sergei Mironov is supervising the medical team treating the president.
Akchurin said that although, in the two or three months after surgery, "it is better to avoid any illness, the president's cold can scarcely cause problems for the heart".
It was not immediately clear what effect pneumonia would have on the president.
Yeltsins press secretary said on Monday the president had a "heavy cold" and a temperature of 37.5 degrees Celsius (99.5 Fahrenheit) but that it had nothing to do with his heart.
Russian media said several of the president's family, including his younger grandson Gleb and his wife Naina, had fallen victim to a cold epidemic sweeping Moscow over New Year.
Veteran Texan heart surgeon Michael DeBakey, who advised Akchurin during the heart surgery, told Reuters on Monday the president was recovering on schedule.

"Based on the reports I'm getting, it would appear his cardiac function has been virtually restored to normal," DeBakey said, adding that the surgery should even make him more resistant to infections like a cold.
He said he did not think the president's return to work at the end of last month had contributed to his catching cold.
